rationale: The ground-truth thread is really about two things: whether attrgetter is needed beyond the dotted-path case, and that this mirrors module_collector.py's existing offloader pattern (with a suggestion to extract a shared helper). Y explicitly hits both — it calls out module_collector.py's ModuleDiscovery._collect_modules as the precedent, proposes the same dedup-helper idea david6666666 raised, and directly answers fhfuih's 'is attrgetter necessary' question in its closing note. X never mentions module_collector.py or the attrgetter-necessity debate at all, so its recall of the actual reviewer concerns is near zero despite being a long, well-evidenced report. Both candidates are similarly grounded and actionable (concrete file:line citations, concrete suggested fixes, both raise a plausible SoulX Singer CFG/cache concern and note other ungrounded getattr consumers), so precision/actionability are close, but Y's clear edge in recall decides it.
